familySensitivity.rationale: The family demonstrates clear asymmetry in sensitivity: exact delivery and complete skips are handled well, but the algorithm overreacts to surged intensity (inserting unnecessary rest) and underreacts to curtailed work. The surge case is particularly problematic because it reduces training volume too aggressively for a single high-intensity session completed successfully 28 days before the event. The curtailed case shows the opposite problem — insufficient recovery response to incomplete high-load work.
algorithmAdjustmentHypotheses: The algorithm's reaction to delivered dose variance is asymmetric: it overreacts to high-intensity surges (surged case) and underreacts to partial completion (curtailed case), while correctly handling exact delivery and complete skips. This suggests the fatigue model weights intensity non-linearly — perhaps too heavily on peak intensity rather than cumulative systemic cost.

The algorithm may be using a threshold-based decision rule that triggers 'overreaction' when any single session exceeds an intensity threshold, without properly accounting for the athlete's overall recovery capacity or remaining training window before the event.

A more robust approach would weight reactions by both the magnitude of deviation AND the time-to-event: small deviations far from the event warrant minimal adjustment, while large deviations close to the event warrant stronger correction. The current algorithm appears to apply uniform reaction strength regardless of timing.

algorithmAdjustmentHypotheses: The algorithm correctly prioritizes objective recovery signals (HRV, RHR) over subjective feelings when they conflict — this is the right behavior for safety.
Race-week plans show strong goal_event_fit scores, indicating the taper logic works well when given sufficient horizon.

algorithmAdjustmentHypotheses: The algorithm correctly distinguishes between heavy lower-body (overreactive) and upper-body/power maintenance (appropriate) perturbations, suggesting that residual fatigue from lower-body strength is negligible when >9 days old with no intervening hard cycling.
